I know the whole "Democratic Socialism" thing is gaining popularity in the US but might I suggest a clearer terminology? Democratic Socialism originally refered to the revisionist marxism of Edouard Bernstein, who proposed that Capitalism ought to be abolished through parliamentary means. I believe social democrat is a more useful term for Bernie, as modern social democracy does not seek to abolish capitalism, and neither does Bernie. I think the distinction is very important. Capitalism has some key elements like wage labour, commodity production, and the private ownership of the means of production, and socialism is best seen in my view as the negation of these core elements. This is not a critique of Bernie but Ithink the terms he use muddy the waters a bit.
